subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Uranus's Tilted Moon System
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Uranus's Tilted Moon System.

hook.text: Uranus spins on its side, tilted 98 degrees. Its moons orbit in the same tilted plane—like a giant spinning top.

buildup.text: This means the moons' poles alternately face the Sun for decades at a time. Seasons are extreme and decades long.

discovery.text: A giant impact likely knocked Uranus onto its side early in solar system history. The moons formed from the resulting debris.

twist.text: Uranus has 28 known moons. All are named after characters from Shakespeare and Alexander Pope—unique in the solar system.

climax.text: The Planetary Decadal Survey ranked a Uranus orbiter as the top priority flagship mission for the coming decade.

punchline.text: A sideways planet with Shakespearean moons. Our top target for the next big mission.

quiz.question: Why do Uranus's moons orbit in a tilted plane?
options: A giant impact likely knocked Uranus on its side, and the moons formed in that plane
Strong magnetic fields from Uranus pull the moons into unusual orbits
The moons were captured from passing asteroids at different angles

details.summary: Uranus rotates nearly on its side (98° tilt), and its 27 known moons orbit in the same tilted plane — unlike any other major planet. This means the moons experience extreme seasons: decades of continuous sunlight at one pole followed by decades of darkness.
details.whyItMatters: Uranus's tilted system demonstrates how catastrophic events can fundamentally alter planetary systems. The extreme seasons experienced by its moons create unique environmental conditions found nowhere else in the solar system.
takeaways: Moons orbit in the plane of Uranus's extreme 98° tilt
Experience decades of continuous sunlight then darkness
Tilt likely caused by an ancient giant impact

faq.question: How does the extreme tilt affect the moons?
faq.answer: Each pole alternates between 42 years of continuous sunlight and 42 years of darkness as Uranus orbits the Sun every 84 years. This creates extreme thermal cycling and seasonal patterns unlike anything else in the solar system.

faq.question: Will we send a mission to study Uranus's moons?
faq.answer: A Uranus orbiter and probe was identified as the top priority flagship mission in the 2022 Planetary Science Decadal Survey. If funded, it could launch in the early 2030s and arrive around 2044, studying Uranus's atmosphere, rings, and moons — our first dedicated mission to this ice giant system…
